hostRules.description: read:packages auth for the private org GitHub Packages NuGet feed (FS.GG.* are not on nuget.org). Lives in this repo's own config — NOT the shared preset — because Renovate does not substitute {{ secrets }} inside presets pulled via extends. Value = org-level Mend App Secret FSGG_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN.

packageRules.description: #300 — NEVER propose FS.GG.UI.* bumps under samples/. The four out-of-solution sample suites map FS.GG.UI.* exclusively to the machine-local feed (see each samples/*/nuget.config packageSourceMapping), which only a local `dotnet pack` of src/ fills, at src/*/*.fsproj <Version>. Renovate's datasource is nuget.pkg.github.com — a feed these projects are configured never to read — so every version it can see is one they cannot resolve (NU1102). That is PR #233: it proposed the published 0.4.0 against a tree pinned to 0.4.0-preview.1 and merged 4/4 green, because nothing in CI read the files it changed. Both halves of that hole are now closed: the required gate checks the pin mirrors <Version>, and packaged-consumer.yml builds the samples against a feed packed from the commit. This rule stops the bot re-proposing, every cycle, a bump the gate now rejects. The pin moves ONLY with the release: commit that moves src <Version>, never on its own.

Do NOT propose bumps to the MATERIALIZED build-config files. Directory.Packages.props and Directory.Build.props are the FS-GG org-shared baseline; they are WRITTEN INTO this tree by the FS.GG.Kit materialize (.config/kit/FS.GG.Kit.receiver.proj, ADR-0062 — the byte-copy scripts/sync-build-config.sh this rule once named is retired) and are marked 'DO NOT EDIT in a consumer repo'. Any local edit is overwritten by the next materialize and reds the REQUIRED Build-config drift gate by design, so a Renovate PR touching them — e.g. the FSharp.Core / dotnet baseline — can NEVER merge; it just churns every cycle and burns a review (see closed #790). Those bumps reach this repo through the FS.GG.Kit pin in Directory.Packages.local.props, which stays managed. Repo-owned pins (SkiaSharp, Expecto, the test SDK, etc.) live there too and stay managed.

.config/dotnet-tools.json WAS ON THE LIST ABOVE AND IS DELIBERATELY OFF IT. FS-GG/.github#1615 (ADR-0068) removed the manifest from the FS.GG.Kit `kit:` block at kit 0.18.0 (#1128), so it is no longer distributed, no longer materialized, and no longer compared byte-for-byte by coordination-coherence — it is this repo's own file, and the drift gate above does not read it. ADR-0068's replacement for the copying is precisely that 'Renovate bumps fs.gg.coord.cli in it directly', so leaving the file on a do-not-propose list would have disabled the one delivery path the decision depends on. THIS ALONE DOES NOT MAKE THAT PATH LIVE, and the honest note belongs here rather than in a commit message nobody re-reads: the org-shared preset this file extends (FS-GG/.github default.json, scoped receives=coordination-kit) still carries its OWN enabled:false for .config/dotnet-tools.json, whose premise — the file is kit-materialized, so a receiver-side bump is a guaranteed-red #794-class PR — is exactly what ADR-0068 removed; FS-GG/.github#1798 is the fix and the ADR records the correction. Removing OUR entry is nevertheless required and comes first, because a repo-local packageRules entry is evaluated after the preset it extends and would keep the file disabled here whatever #1798 does. It is deliberately NOT re-enabled with a local override: that would be this repo restating an org rule the hub is already correcting (ADR-0058), and a bump proposed here today would still be judged by a preset that says no. fake-cli is the single exception, and it is PINNED rather than managed: its version must equal the Fake.Core.* library pin in Directory.Packages.local.props and build.fsx.lock (6.1.4 — specs/213 INV-5/C-5), NOTHING in CI asserts that equality, and the compiled-FAKE front-end this repo actually builds with reads the library pin, not the tool. A lone tool bump would therefore go green while quietly breaking the invariant. Move the three together in one hand-authored PR, or not at all.

Move Expecto and its test-SDK adapter as one unit — they must stay version-compatible, so they bump together in a single PR rather than as two that momentarily conflict. This is what makes the Expecto 11 move land as one coherent PR now that the cap is gone (#845). The cap this rule used to wait on ('Expecto is capped to the 10.x line…, ACTION WHEN YoloDev.Expecto.TestSdk ships a release supporting Expecto >= 11: delete this allowedVersions cap') was RETIRED by its own stated trigger: adapter 0.16.0 depends on Expecto 10.2.3 as a MINIMUM with no upper bound (verified against the nuspec on api.nuget.org, not inferred from the version number), and this repo has been on 0.16.0 for some time — so the adapter had stopped constraining Expecto and the cap was the only thing holding it at 10.x. What still needs saying is the part the cap did NOT: the adapter's own latest, 1.0.0, is a DOWNGRADE — it depends on Expecto [9.0.0, 10.0.0), a HIGHER number on an OLDER lineage, and 0.16.0 in the middle is the only version that admits Expecto 11. Renovate reads versions, not lineages. That fact is now enforced for every repo by `allowedVersions: <1.0.0` on YoloDev.Expecto.TestSdk in the SHARED preset (FS-GG/.github default.json, .github#850) rather than six times over, which is what makes deleting the cap here safe — deleting it while the adapter was uncapped would have let Renovate propose 1.0.0 and force Expecto back to 9.x (NU1608, warning-as-error).
